summary: Initialized active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for exact placeholder feature token `<fff>`, registered it in ledger_registry.json, captured the collaborator planning persona and ledger-only constraints, and opened q-0001 to ask what we are working on before accepting product requirements.

User clarified that `<fff>` means evaluating dmtrKovalenko/fff, OpenCode's recent fff support, and Cursor's fast regex search approach to decide whether fff-style functionality would benefit Puppet Master. Confirmed local Plans already document Cursor-style indexed regex acceleration as Instant Grep / SparseNgramIndex, and captured fff as a potential fuzzy/frecency file discovery complement rather than a replacement for PM's existing regex-index canon.

Explained the distinction between native fff-inspired file discovery as a PM-owned product direction and a direct fff dependency/prototype as a faster integration/proof path. Captured pros, cons, and a recommendation to treat native ownership as the long-term direction while allowing a bounded direct-fff prototype for evidence.

Jared chose `Let’s do native`, authorized cloning fff and OpenCode for implementation inspection, and required the cloned repos to be deleted afterwards. Inspected dmtrKovalenko/fff at commit 957f222da76f120868defdf9e7204309c3800e5e and anomalyco/opencode at commit cf31029350820c6bfc0fbd0e052a79a067ee6116. Captured native PM-owned file-discovery API, ranking, lifecycle, guardrail, UI-ordering, and validation lessons; clones remain temporary evidence only and must be deleted before response completion.

Jared answered q-0003: native fff-inspired file discovery should be `one shared substrate for both agent tools and GUI surfaces from day one`. Captured this as an accepted product direction, moved the agent/tool and GUI discovery candidates into accepted shared-substrate scope, opened q-0004 to choose the first concrete acceptance workflow, and kept compile queue empty pending explicit compile permission.

Jared clarified that Orchestrator, Executor, WorkNodes, Planning Wizard, PRDBuilder, Assistant Chat, and `anything that uses an agent` should be able to discover files through the shared native discovery substrate. Captured this as a broad consumer-contract requirement and kept q-0004 open for selecting a concrete first acceptance scenario.

Jared agreed with the constructive push that the broad agent-bearing scope needs a conformance contract, not just a feature. Captured the requirement that every agent-bearing surface prove it can call the shared discovery substrate, receive ranked/fresh/fallback-aware results, and respect the same FileSafe, permissions, ignore, and policy envelope.

In response to Jared asking `what do you think?`, recommended anchoring the first acceptance example on an agent context-acquisition workflow that begins in Assistant Chat, uses the shared substrate for ranked/fresh/policy-aware file discovery, feeds Planning Wizard/PRDBuilder context selection, and proves Orchestrator, Executor, and WorkNode consumers use the same conformance contract without creating WorkNodes in the ledger phase.

Jared clarified that agents should use the shared native discovery substrate while working on ordinary tasks, such as fixing a bug and needing to locate the right section of code in the repo. Captured this as the first acceptance workflow and as a stronger ambient/default agent code-discovery requirement than OpenCode's current service-layer integration.

Jared asked to pull in the OpenCode repo to know exactly how it uses fff. Cloned anomalyco/opencode current HEAD c5a4a8288cbe115f673f3f9933fe217402c85406 into /tmp, inspected the fff/search/autocomplete/tool paths, confirmed fff is used behind FileSystem/Search and file-discovery surfaces while model-facing grep/glob tools still use ripgrep directly, then deleted the temporary clone.

Jared asked whether there is enough to make the feature implementation-ready in the ledger. Assessed that the ledger has enough for an implementation-ready tightening pass under explicit assumptions: native PM-owned substrate, ambient default agent repo orientation, ordinary bug-fix/code-orientation as first acceptance workflow, OpenCode as reference rather than parity target, and exact verification after ranked discovery. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared answered the implementation-ready tightening question with `ok lets get to it`. Captured the ledger-only implementation contract for native PM-owned fff-inspired discovery: shared DiscoveryService substrate, request/result/provenance shapes, ambient agent invocation rules, consumer conformance matrix, FileSafe/permissions/ignore/fallback policy envelope, ranking model, exact verification handoff, lifecycle/freshness behavior, validation scenarios, non-goals, and candidate owner hints. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized and the compile queue stays empty.

Jared asked, `Before we convert this to the plans, are there any gaps, or anything underspecced you can find?` Reviewed the implementation-ready ledger packet against the accepted atoms and live owner maps. Found that the product direction is strong but several compile-readiness details remain underspecified: file/path versus content-search scope, exact typed enums and event/receipt names, owner/consumer/doc-impact matrix, frecency persistence/privacy/reset controls, remote/worktree/cache behavior, resource budgets, GUI states, side-channel leakage semantics, ambient agent tool-selection receipts, and exact conformance rows. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized and should wait until these gaps are resolved or explicitly accepted as assumptions.

Jared said `ok lets work through them` and added that for the GUI, discovery should also show what it is doing in the Assistant Chat threads. Recorded recommended candidate resolutions for the open pre-compile questions covering scope, remote/cache/worktree behavior, frecency privacy defaults, and tool/event vocabulary. Recorded Assistant Chat thread discovery visibility as an accepted GUI requirement: discovery, fallback, policy, and exact-verification activity must be visible in Assistant Chat thread activity, not hidden only in logs.

Jared continued the gap-resolution conversation and added that there should be a GUI setting to turn off showing discovery activity in Assistant Chat. Captured an accepted setting requirement: discovery activity is visible in Assistant Chat threads by default for transparency, but a GUI setting can hide routine inline discovery activity. The toggle must not suppress permission prompts, denied/hidden-by-policy safety messaging, durable receipts, or auditability.

Jared said `those defaults look good` and added that native discovery `needs to work over ssh too`. Closed q-0006 through q-0009 as answered, promoted the four candidate defaults to accepted, and added SSH-backed project roots as a first-class discovery requirement. SSH discovery must use the remote project identity and policy envelope, avoid silent local fallback, disclose cache/fallback freshness, and preserve exact verification and Assistant Chat visibility semantics.

Jared said `ok go ahead` after the accepted gap resolutions. Materialized ledger-only pre-compile matrices at state/doc_impact_matrix.json and state/consumer_conformance_matrix.json. The doc-impact matrix maps future PlanUnit slugs to primary owner docs, supporting owners, consumer docs, compile obligations, backlink obligations, and do-not-touch constraints. The consumer-conformance matrix records exact conformance rows for Assistant Chat, @file/file mentions, Quick Open, Search path narrowing, File Manager, Planning Wizard, PRDBuilder, Orchestrator, Executor, future WorkNode intake, shared discover_paths, remote/SSH adapter, and runtime artifact/audit receipt browsing. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared asked `any more gaps?` after the pre-compile matrices were materialized. Reviewed the ledger-source package, doc-impact matrix, and consumer-conformance matrix for missing owners, missing obligations, missing GUI classification, missing consumer request/result/fallback/receipt/validation behavior, missing owner docs, and remaining underspecified product decisions. No blocking product, owner-routing, or consumer-conformance gaps remain before an explicit compile request. Remaining precision items are non-blocking compile or implementation obligations: enumerate exact schema/event values, set performance/resource budgets, specify deterministic ranking and tie-breaker/tuning behavior, choose SSH implementation topology without weakening remote identity/no-local-fallback constraints, and place/name the Assistant Chat discovery-visibility GUI setting. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared said `ok address those issues`. Resolved the five post-matrix precision obligations in ledger-only form and materialized state/precision_contract.json. Accepted exact DiscoveryRequest/DiscoveryResult/receipt enum and field values; performance/resource budgets for warm query, GUI query, agent discover_paths, cold index, remote/SSH, watcher/reindex/cancellation, memory, and disk; deterministic ranking weights, penalties, tie-breakers, and privacy handling; SSH topology as local DiscoveryService plus SSH remote manifest adapter with no persistent remote daemon required for MVP and no silent local substitution; and Assistant Chat setting placement/copy as Settings > Assistant Chat > Activity > Show file discovery activity in chat. Updated doc-impact and consumer-conformance matrices with source refs and compile obligations. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared asked `Is there anything else we should look at, anything else missing from the implimentation? Any more gaps?` Reviewed state/precision_contract.json, the doc-impact and consumer-conformance matrices, and relevant owner-doc signals for implementation-slice ambiguity. No new product-direction blocker was found, but seven second-order implementation gaps should be resolved or explicitly accepted as defaults before build: rollout/kill-switch/degraded fallback; cross-platform path normalization and display identity; index/cache schema versioning and rebuild policy; ambient discovery concurrency/backpressure/deduplication; SSH auth/host-authority alignment; frecency/history/receipt retention and deletion semantics; and migration of existing GUI fuzzy/file-search routes without duplicate ranking. Recorded these as candidate atoms atom-0081 through atom-0087 and open questions q-0010 through q-0016. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared said `ok sounds good`, accepting the seven recommended second-order implementation defaults. Promoted atom-0081 through atom-0087 to accepted and closed q-0010 through q-0016 as answered: rollout/kill switch, canonical path identity/display normalization, index/cache schema versioning and rebuild policy, shared scheduler/backpressure, SSH auth/remote host authority, frecency/history/receipt retention, and GUI fuzzy/file-search route migration through DiscoveryService. Canonical Plans compile remains unauthorized.

Jared requested one last deeper audit using multiple subagents and a second sweep. Five read-only audit agents plus the main-thread sweep found enum/case drift, stale post-evt-0021 matrix routing, shared schema owner-routing risk, no-leak count/id underspecification, SSH permission/host-trust field gaps, ambient invocation scope-bleed risk, Assistant Chat visibility toggle safety-boundary wording, WorkNode future-boundary overread risk, validator blind spots for readiness artifacts, and compile/governance readiness wording that was too strong. Reconciled these findings in ledger-only state artifacts and records; canonical Plans, PlanUnit indexes, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, and auto_decisions remain untouched and unauthorized.

Jared asked whether anything more needs to be addressed in the ledger. Re-read current/open/compile projections, reran the bootstrap ledger validator, and reran the targeted semantic checks for atom reachability, stale enum tokens, missing precision values, missing owner docs, and deep-audit second-sweep status. No new ledger-internal product, owner-routing, enum, GUI-classification, consumer-conformance, or compile-reachability gaps were found. Remaining caveats are explicit and unchanged: generated governance evidence drift belongs to a separate explicit governance seal/refresh lane, and readiness artifacts remain manual/source-lineage until validator/schema support is added.

Jared asked again whether anything more needs to be addressed in the ledger. Re-read the current/open/compile/deep-audit projections and reran the bootstrap ledger validator. The validator passed with 95 atoms, 16 decisions, 16 questions, zero compile queue items, zero errors, and zero warnings. No new ledger-internal gap was found. Remaining caveats are unchanged: generated governance evidence drift belongs to a separate explicit governance seal/refresh lane, and readiness artifacts remain manual/source-lineage until validator/schema support is added.

All four read-only compile-placement subagent proposals were received and preserved in state/subagent_compile_proposals.json. Compiled accepted native PM-owned fff-inspired discovery atoms into live non-pipeline Plans PlanUnits across 19 owner docs; updated existing T-072 and created 24 new PlanUnits; regenerated allowed Plans/.plan_index outputs with no WorkNodes or NodeSeed candidates.
